name: MathlibAnnex.Satellite.satellitePolynomial
title: A weighted determinant polynomial with satellites

content.display_title: A weighted determinant polynomial with satellites
content.one_sentence_role: Adds linear row-replacement contributions to a base determinant.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $V=\mathbb R^n$ with reference sup norm, and $J$ a finite index set. Let $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ be a family of continuous real linear functionals on $V$, and $s=(s_a)_{a\in J}$ another such family. Choose $w\in\mathbb R$ and coefficients $c_a\in V$. Let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be the standard coordinate vectors. Put $M_F=(\ell_i(e_j))_{i,j}$ and replace row $i$ by $(s_a(e_j))_j$ when writing $M_F[i\leftarrow s_a]$.
content.definition_explanation:
The full defining expression is
$$\Phi_{w,c}(F,s)=w\det M_F+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a].$$
Both sums are finite. If $J$ is empty, only $w\det M_F$ remains. If $n=0$, the empty determinant is $1$ and the inner sum is empty, so the value is $w$.
content.assumptions: Only the finite indices, the real weight, coefficient vectors and the two families of continuous linear functionals are inputs. There is no norm model $p$, contraction condition, positive-weight hypothesis or invertibility hypothesis.
content.conclusion: The definition returns the scalar $\Phi_{w,c}(F,s)$. The satellites are additional dual functionals, not vectors or points of a net.
content.lean_realization_notes: The private coordinate and row-replacement aliases in [the exact local aliases](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L13-L23) identify reference vectors, frame rows, and standard-basis matrices. They do not restrict the defining polynomial to admissible configurations; such a restriction is imposed only in later theorems.
